sections.content:
The drag didn't work either. Nothing changes. Hmm.
Let me rethink. Maybe the arrow keys do move the player, but the player is invisible / not drawn, or the arrow keys move a "cursor" that's hard to see. board_changed=False means the board is identical. So no.
Maybe I need to click a specific cell of the 3×3 grid to toggle it. Let me try clicking a gray cell, e.g. (50,25) (top-left g). If it toggles to white, that would confirm the grid is interactive.
Or click the purple panel.
Or maybe the game requires clicking the small blue+sky marker at the right end (the "goal")?
Let me think about what kind of game this is. 64x64 grid, level 1. Elements:
1. Slider: blue square + gray bar + blue/sky marker at the right end.
2. 3×3 grid of white/gray cells (checkerboard).
3. Purple panel with a plus-cross and 4 purple dots.
This might be a "pattern completion" game: the purple panel shows a pattern, and the 3×3 grid needs to be toggled to match it. But the grid already matches... unless the white cells represent "filled" and the pattern's dots represent the cells that should be filled — in which case it's already solved, which is weird.
Wait, maybe I should look more carefully. The purple panel: a gray plus shape (48 pixels) with purple dots at N/W/E/S. Actually, the gray plus shape is the "background" of the panel, and the purple dots are the pattern. The 3×3 grid: white cells at top-center, middle-left, middle-right, bottom-center.
Hmm, what if the goal is the opposite: to make the grid match the pattern, and the current grid is a checkerboard where the white cells are at the plus positions... they match. So maybe the level's goal is something else entirely, and the grid is a "palette" or "keypad."
Another idea: this might be a game where you use arrow keys to move the blue square, but the square is on a track and only moves when... no, that's not it.
Let me look at the ASCII of the whole board to check if there's anything I'm missing (like a thin line or a small object). The segmentation only had 23 nodes. The black background node 0 has children [2,3,4,5,6,11] — everything else is inside the background. Node 1 is the green bar.
Let me check the green bar: N (light green), columns 62-63, rows 0-63. This is probably a timer/progress bar.
Maybe the game is: click a cell of the 3×3 grid to toggle white/gray, and the goal is to make the grid all white (or match the pattern). Let me try clicking a gray cell.
Actually, wait. Let me reconsider the slider. The blue square is at the left end of the gray bar, and the gray bar has a notch: the boundary of node 4 shows [[19,17],[19,38],[22,38],[22,23],[21,23],[20,22],[20,17]] — the bar is 4 rows tall (19-22) from columns 17-38, but rows 20-21 only from column 22? Let me reread: the boundary is clockwise: (19,17) → (19,38) → (22,38) → (22,23) → (21,23) → (20,22) → (20,17) → back to (19,17). So the shape is: rows 19-20: columns 17-38? Hmm: from (19,17) to (19,38) is the top edge. Down to (22,38): right edge. Left to (22,23): bottom edge at row 22 up to column 23. Up to (21,23), left to (20,22), up to (20,17), and then to (19,17). So the bar is 4 rows tall (19-22) in columns 23-38, and in columns 17-22 it's only rows 19-20 (2 rows tall). So the track is thicker on the right side. Interesting — this is a "track" with a raised portion.
Actually, from the ASCII:
Row 19: BBbSSSSggggggggggggggggggggggbbSSBBB — g from column 17 to column 38
Row 20: BBbSSSSggggggggggggggggggggggbbSSBBB — g from column 17 to column 38
Row 21: BBbSSSSBBBBBBggggggggggggggggbbSSBBB — g from column 23 to column 38
Row 22: BBbbbbbBBBBBBggggggggggggggggbbSSBBB — g from column 23 to column 38
So the track: rows 19-20 are full width (columns 17-38), rows 21-22 are only columns 23-38. So the blue square (rows 17-22) sits on top of the left portion of the track.
Hmm, this looks like a "handle" shape: a blue square with a long handle extending to the right, with the handle's lower half extending further. Like a key or a lever.
The blue+sky marker at the right end (columns 39-42, rows 19-22) is 2×2 blue + 2×2 sky, 4 rows tall.
This strongly resembles a slider control where the knob (blue square) is at the left end and the goal is to slide it to the right end where the marker is.
But neither the arrow keys nor the drag worked. Maybe the mouse coordinates need to be exact, or maybe the drag needs to be done in a single action sequence with intermediate points? Or maybe the game uses MOUSE as "click and hold," and the arrow keys move while held? That's complex.
Or maybe I'm misreading, and the actual player is somewhere else, and the arrow keys do move it, but the movement is 1 pixel and board_changed... no, board_changed was False.
Let me try clicking a cell of the 3×3 grid. If nothing happens there either, try clicking the purple panel.
Actually, let me reconsider: maybe the game is a "Simon"-style or "light up" game where you click cells to toggle them, and the goal is to make the grid match the pattern (all white? or the plus pattern?). The grid currently shows a plus pattern in white. The purple panel shows a plus pattern in purple dots. If the goal is "make the grid all white," I need to toggle the 5 gray cells.
Let me try clicking a gray cell at (50,25).
